summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge: analyze Soony's launch data, build a general recheck-and-act agent product (poller, extraction, recompute, supplier emails with approval), and prepare for office-hours interviews and live supplier interactions.
summary.outcome: Found that Soony's plan says 'ok' while the Collector's Edition misses Sunday (overbooked art books, failed statues, sleeve rev conflict, card shortfall). Built and committed a versioned watcher, reconciled shipment tracking, an editable email review, a sent-folder duplicate guard, and drop-rehearsal fixes. Produced briefing docs and pages, and sent real supplier emails. Final step was committing the drop-drill work, which an earlier commit had half-picked-up.

repo: The portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no webhooks, so new drops must be detected by polling and comparing SHA-256 checksums. Files can be replaced under the same name.
The team shares one mailbox. The app only sees mail it sent itself, so hand-sent mail and Lucas's Pulse console mail are invisible unless the sent folder is read.

Lucas's branch origin/new-approach (pulse-console/server.mjs) sends mail through the shared mailbox without the supplier allow-list. It sent confusing emails to Hwaseong and one to an external Gmail address.
Supplier profiles hold real contact names. Hand-written emails should use the full profile name, not a salutation guessed from the address.
Supplier JSON profiles (status 'watch'/'at risk') contradict the CSV profiles that say 'active', and the app originally read only email addresses from them.
Team workflow lives in CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md in the repo. Tasks are claimed with a 'Now' line in PROGRESS.md.
Data and notes are confidential and kept in the gitignored data/ folder. .env is gitignored and .env.example is committed.

Drill findings: a renamed CSV column made the verifier read stock as zero and silently auto-resolved 3 real cards. The predictor wrote impacts.json keyed by event while papercheck expected a list, which crashed the whole pipeline.

code.finding: New file that compares newer supplier profiles with profile.csv and raises cards. It was imported by uncommitted api.py edits that got swept into commit b0cff82, so that commit alone would fail at import.

New module that syncs the shared mailbox's sent folder to cases. Matching goes by thread reference, then supplier plus order number, then a part number that fits exactly one case. It feeds a 12-hour duplicate-send guard that returns 409 unless the user chooses 'Send anyway'.

Reconciles shipment status by precedence: goods receipt, site answer, supplier doc or email, hand-kept tracker, system export, other sheets. It never moves a shipment backwards and picks the highest tracker version, then the newest file.

workflow: Entire only writes a checkpoint when repo files change, so 'no files modified' turns are skipped by design.
Long-running work was delegated to subagents on copies of the data. Their uncommitted edits can be swept into the main session's commits, so stage files explicitly.
Unrequested emails need care: the app's approval flow, allow-lists and duplicate guards matter because the mailbox is shared and sends reach real suppliers.
Screenshot checks of UI changes, plus tests, tsc and ruff before each commit, caught wording and layout bugs such as a button forcing a line break.

friction: Shared mailbox caused a double order to Karton Nowak (the app at 06:50, someone by hand at 07:04) and stray Pulse emails to Hwaseong.
Three hand-written supplier emails guessed salutations from addresses and two were wrong (Mr Nowak, Mr Rohan).
The first commit b0cff82 accidentally included subagent edits that depend on an untracked file.
The sign-off rule sent every costed case to Maren, stricter than the policy limits.
The portal login was pasted into Discord history.
A UI claim sentence read badly and the source link button forced a stray period onto its own line.
The 11-minute-class timing pressure, lottery-assigned office hours and the 24-hour Nowak offer limited what could be done.
open_items: Commit supplier_master.py and the drill work together (in progress at the end of the transcript), leaving the UX expert's files out.
Decide whether to send Hwaseong a note disregarding the three Pulse test emails, and draft a message to Lucas about the missing allow-list and the email to an external Gmail address.
Use the policy approval limits (who may approve how much) instead of routing every costed case to Maren.
The rev B PackRight card should incorporate Lin Hui's reply (needs the rev C PDF and a formal change notice, reprint costs per §6.2).
Routine diagram UX redesign (one trigger, 'Only if' list, funnel counts, trust switch below) is still in progress with a UX agent.
A real predictor run is untested (it defaults to gpt-5 on the OpenAI key and costs money), and the memo's Quality & Compliance and air/rush escalation rules are extracted but not used for routing.
A renamed stock column still makes the verifier read stock as zero, with only the datacheck warning as a signal.
The verifier may double-count 28,000 cards already received on 21 Nov, and floor.receipts() treats any receipt on the same order and part as booked regardless of date.
Internal email addresses (Maren, Hamburg receiving) are missing, so colleague CC is not possible.
Header edits in the review sheet are not carried by a spoken 'yes'.
Ask Lio engineers whether portal data is identical across teams and whether supplier replies create portal files.
Decide whether to delete the earlier Claude doc now that the briefing page exists.
